title: Serre vanishing for a finite graded module on a proper scheme
statement: Let $A$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}B_n$ be a finitely generated graded commutative $A$-algebra (the grading has $B_iB_j\subseteq B_{i+j}$; no condition $B_0=A$ or generation in degree one is imposed). Let $\widetilde B$ be the quasi-coherent algebra associated to $B$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module] and put $\mathcal B=f^*\widetilde B$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $\mathcal G$ is a finite type graded quasi-coherent $\mathcal B$-module (locally admitting a surjection from a finite direct sum of graded shifts of $\mathcal B$), and $\mathcal L$ is an ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] on $X$, then there is $d_0$ such that $H^p(X,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})=0$ for all $p>0$ and $d\ge d_0$, tensor products are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $H^p$ is sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0897 (lemma-graded-finiteness), part (2), using Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample), proper pushforward finiteness, and the Serre vanishing argument

proof.text: Forget the grading. The hypothesis of graded finite type supplies local finite generating sections of the underlying $\mathcal B$-module. Form $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(B)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}X$ with projections $\pi:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}(B)$. The morphism $\pi$ is affine, since it is the base change of a morphism of affine schemes. Properness of $f'$ follows by base change. Since $B$ is a finite type algebra over Noetherian $A$, it is Noetherian, and $X'$ is Noetherian because $f'$ is proper, hence finite type.

On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\subseteq X$, $\pi^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_A B)$; the associated-algebra and pullback constructions identify $\mathcal B|_U$ with the sheaf associated to $R\otimes_A B$. Thus $X'$ is the relative spectrum of $\mathcal B$, and $\pi_*\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal B$. By the affine module correspondence choose $\mathcal G'$ quasi-coherent with $\pi_*\mathcal G'=\mathcal G$. Finite type is preserved by that correspondence, so $\mathcal G'$ is finite type; since $X'$ is locally Noetherian, it is coherent.

Set $\mathcal L'=\pi^*\mathcal L$. Pullback along the affine morphism $\pi$ preserves ampleness. Apply coherent Serre vanishing to $f'$, $\mathcal G'$ and $\mathcal L'$: there is one $d_0\ge0$ with $H^p(X',\mathcal G'\otimes(\mathcal L')^{\otimes d})=0$ for all $p>0$, $d\ge d_0$.

For every $d\ge0$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\pi_*(\mathcal G'\otimes\pi^*\mathcal L^{\otimes d})=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$. To verify it, take an open set on which $\mathcal L$ is free of rank one. Both sides identify with $\pi_*\mathcal G'$ there; changing the generator by a unit $a$ multiplies both identifications by the same $a^d$, so the identifications glue. The same trivializations show $(\pi^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes d}=\pi^*(\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$.

The tensor product upstairs is quasi-coherent: on the same trivializing opens it equals $\mathcal G'$. The affine cohomology edge isomorphism for $\pi$ therefore identifies $H^p(X,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$ with $H^p(X',\mathcal G'\otimes(\mathcal L')^{\otimes d})$. The latter vanishes by Step 3 for every $p>0$ and $d\ge d_0$, proving the assertion.
